Buffers the whole input relation, runs Splink's Fellegi-Sunter model with fuzzy (Jaro-Winkler / Levenshtein) comparisons over the chosen columns, links record pairs above a match-probability threshold, and returns the input rows unchanged plus an appended cluster_id (rows sharing one are the same real-world entity) and match_probability. rows.vgi.doc_llm: Probabilistic entity resolution over a whole SQL relation. Pass a relation of records as the first positional argument (a `(SELECT ...)` subquery) and name the comparison columns with `columns := 'col1,col2,...'`. The function buffers every input row, runs Splink's Fellegi-Sunter model with fuzzy comparisons (Jaro-Winkler on name-like columns, Levenshtein elsewhere), links candidate pairs above `threshold` (default 0.5), and assigns each row a `cluster_id` (rows sharing one are the same real-world entity) plus a `match_probability`. Every input column is returned unchanged. Use it to deduplicate customer/contact/product lists or to link records that refer to the same entity. Inputs: the relation, `columns`, optional `threshold` and `train` (opt-in unsupervised EM, weak on tiny inputs). Edge cases: an empty relation raises an error; singletons get their own cluster_id and a match_probability of 1.0; an input column already named `cluster_id` or `match_probability` is replaced by the produced one.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# match_resolve

Cluster the rows of a relation into **resolved entities** (deduplication / record linkage) using probabilistic matching.

## What it does

Buffers the whole input relation, scores every candidate record pair with [Splink](https://github.com/moj-analytical-services/splink)'s Fellegi-Sunter model (fuzzy Jaro-Winkler / Levenshtein comparisons), links pairs above the threshold, and groups linked records into clusters.

## Calling it

Signature: `match_resolve(relation, columns := '...', threshold := 0.5, train := false)`. The first positional argument is the relation to resolve, passed as a parenthesised subquery over your source rows; the runnable, coverage-checked examples are attached to this function's example set.

- `columns` — comma-separated comparison columns to match on (required).
- `threshold` — match-probability cutoff in `[0,1]` for linking pairs (default `0.5`).
- `train` — opt into Splink's unsupervised EM refinement (default `false`; weak on tiny inputs).

## Returns

Every input column unchanged, plus `cluster_id` (`VARCHAR`) and `match_probability` (`DOUBLE`).

## Notes

- Singletons get their own `cluster_id` and `match_probability = 1.0`.
- An empty input relation raises an error.
- This is a buffer-all-then-compute operator; block tightly for very large inputs.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Dedup on name + email; the John/Jon Smith rows share a cluster_id, Jane Doe is separate.", "sql": "SELECT first_name, last_name, email, cluster_id, match_probability FROM match.main.match_resolve((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('John','Smith','john@x.com'),('Jon','Smith','john@x.com'),('Jane','Doe','jane@y.com')) AS t(first_name,last_name,email)), columns := 'first_name,last_name,email') ORDER BY cluster_id, first_name"}, {"description": "Build a golden record per entity: resolve the built-in sample_customers demo on name + email and collapse each cluster to one row (lowest record_id, the first-name spellings seen, email, city, and how many source records merged) -- the three Smith variants and two Doe variants each become one row, the two Jones stay separate.", "sql": "SELECT min(record_id) AS golden_record_id, string_agg(DISTINCT first_name, ' / ' ORDER BY first_name) AS name_variants, any_value(last_name) AS last_name, any_value(email) AS email, any_value(city) AS city, count(*) AS source_records FROM match.main.match_resolve((SELECT record_id, first_name, last_name, email, city FROM match.main.sample_customers), columns := 'first_name,last_name,email') GROUP BY cluster_id ORDER BY golden_record_id"}, {"description": "Score the resolver against sample_customers' ground-truth expected_entity label: self-join the resolved rows into record pairs and count true/false positive and false negative links, with pairwise precision and recall (4 true links, no false ones: precision = recall = 1.0).", "sql": "WITH resolved AS (SELECT record_id, expected_entity, cluster_id FROM match.main.match_resolve((SELECT record_id, first_name, last_name, email, expected_entity FROM match.main.sample_customers), columns := 'first_name,last_name,email')), pairs AS (SELECT a.cluster_id = b.cluster_id AS predicted_same, a.expected_entity = b.expected_entity AS actually_same FROM resolved AS a JOIN resolved AS b ON a.record_id < b.record_id) SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE predicted_same AND actually_same) AS true_pos, count(*) FILTER (WHERE predicted_same AND NOT actually_same) AS false_pos, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT predicted_same AND actually_same) AS false_neg, round(true_pos / nullif(true_pos + false_pos, 0), 3) AS precision, round(true_pos / nullif(true_pos + false_neg, 0), 3) AS recall FROM pairs"}, {"description": "Check what dropping email costs: resolve sample_customers on first + last name only at threshold 0.7 and count clusters per ground-truth entity -- Jane/Janet Doe still link, but the John/Jon/Johnny Smith variants split into three clusters (under-merging).", "sql": "SELECT expected_entity, count(*) AS records, count(DISTINCT cluster_id) AS clusters FROM match.main.match_resolve((SELECT record_id, first_name, last_name, expected_entity FROM match.main.sample_customers), columns := 'first_name,last_name', threshold := 0.7) GROUP BY expected_entity ORDER BY expected_entity"}, {"description": "Surface only duplicate groups by clustering and keeping entities with more than one record.", "sql": "SELECT cluster_id, count(*) AS rows_in_entity FROM match.main.match_resolve((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('John','Smith','john@x.com'),('Jon','Smith','john@x.com'),('Jane','Doe','jane@y.com'),('Jayne','Doe','jane@y.com'),('Bob','Ng','bob@z.com')) AS t(first_name,last_name,email)), columns := 'first_name,last_name,email') GROUP BY cluster_id HAVING count(*) > 1 ORDER BY rows_in_entity DESC"}, {"description": "Stricter resolution: raise the link threshold and keep only the more-confident matches.", "sql": "SELECT first_name, last_name, cluster_id, match_probability FROM match.main.match_resolve((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('John','Smith','john@x.com'),('Jon','Smith','john@x.com'),('Jane','Doe','jane@y.com')) AS t(first_name,last_name,email)), columns := 'first_name,last_name,email', threshold := 0.9) WHERE match_probability >= 0.5 ORDER BY cluster_id, first_name"}]

rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The result schema is **dynamic**: it is the input relation's own columns, passed through unchanged, followed by two appended columns. The passthrough columns therefore vary with whatever relation you pass as the first argument; the two appended columns are always present. If the input already has a `cluster_id` or `match_probability` column, it is replaced by the produced one.

### Appended columns (always present)

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| cluster_id | VARCHAR | Resolved-entity id; rows sharing a cluster_id are the same entity (a singleton entity gets its own id). |
| match_probability | DOUBLE | Strongest pairwise match probability linking the row into its cluster, in [0, 1] (1.0 for a singleton). |

### Passthrough columns (vary by input) — shown for the (first_name, last_name, email) demo relation

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| first_name | VARCHAR | Echo of the like-named input column (a comparison column in this demo). |
| last_name | VARCHAR | Echo of the like-named input column (a comparison column in this demo). |
| email | VARCHAR | Echo of the like-named input column (a comparison column in this demo). |
